Santa Ana. I had a room there till I lost it, then it was the bridge and the washes for a while.
Santa Ana, and then the bridge and the washes. Thank you for telling me. Do you have an ID or any papers with your name on them right now?

Sixty-two.

You count. You don't have to know what you need yet. We can just start with what's ahead of you. When you leave here, where do you think you'll sleep?
Honestly, I don't know yet. Maybe my cousin's couch if she still has it, or the shelter over on Fifth if I can't.
Okay, a couch with your cousin or the shelter on Fifth. Got it. Do you know how you'll get around when you leave, like walking, stairs, or a bus?
Mostly walking, I guess. I can handle the bus if I have to, but my knee's been bad lately, so stairs take a while.
Okay, walking, the bus if you need it, and stairs are slow because of your knee. Thanks for telling me. Where did you live before you came here?
I was staying in a room over on the east side of town, but I lost it a couple months back when the rent went up and I fell behind.
I'm sorry the rent went up and you lost your room. Got it, the east side of town. What city was that in?
Same place, Orange County. Anaheim, I think, right on the edge where it runs up toward Fullerton.
Anaheim, near Fullerton. Got it. Do you have an ID or any papers with your name on them right now?
I've got a California ID card, the old kind, and it's in my wallet somewhere. The discharge papers, though, I don't have those. I think my mom had them and I never got them back.
Got it. You have a California ID in your wallet, and your discharge papers are with your mom. Do you have a phone you can use right now, or is that something you're still working on?
I've got a flip phone, but it's almost dead and I don't have the charger with me. My cousin's number is in it, though.

Ask the DMV or a homeless services provider. Applicants still have to prove identity and, for a first California card, residency; that is often the real obstacle.

sources.notes: Text-line hours are from the 211OC home page. The OC HMIS site (https://ochmis.org/) shows a different number for the same referral service, 949-646-4357. Some phones cannot dial 2-1-1; the FAQ says to use the toll-free number instead.
